safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Reduce SAP safety lead time from 3.0 to 1.96 days

narrative: Material PL1__M17AF202 exhibits variable daily demand (CV=0.51, mean=4,646 units/day) with no statistically significant trend across the observation window March 2025–March 2026. Lead times are moderately stable (CV=0.47, mean=2.66 days) with transport variability as the dominant risk driver (60% of LT variance). The recommended (r,Q) continuous-review policy uses an EOQ-derived order quantity of 31,198 units and a safety stock of 11,426 units, raising the reorder point to 23,791 units to sustain the 95% service level. This reduces annual orders from ~1,107 to ~37, yielding a 90.9% reduction in total inventory cost.
warnings: SAP order quantity (1,045 = MOQ) is far below EOQ (31,198); excessive ordering frequency detected.
SAP safety stock (3,393) is below analytically recommended level (11,426); service level risk under current policy.
Safety lead time reduced from SAP 3.0 days to recommended 1.96 days — update ERP parameter.

research_insights.selected_model: (r,Q) — Fixed reorder point, fixed order quantity (continuous review, EOQ-based)
research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is moderately variable with no trend, and lead times are stable enough for a fixed reorder point. The (r,Q) policy minimises total replenishment cost by balancing ordering and holding costs via EOQ, while the safety stock formula accounts for joint demand and lead time uncertainty at the 95% service level.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Capacity constraint is non-binding: SS(11,426) + OQ(31,198) = 42,624 <= max_storage(53,952). Headroom of ~11,328 units. No immediate storage risk detected.
research_insights.escalation_flag: None — MOQ + safety stock is well within capacity. No infeasibility conflict.
